headline: QatarEnergy acquires 25% stake in Sintana-exposed PEL 82 offshore Namibia
<<<SUMMARY>>>
Sintana Energy CEO Robert Bose joined Steve Darling from Proactive to discuss QatarEnergy's agreement to acquire a 25% participating interest in Petroleum Exploration Licence 82 (PEL 82), offshore Namibia, from an affiliate of Chevron Corporation. The transaction brings another major international energy company into the licence, while leaving the interests held by Sintana Energy and its subsidiary, Custos Energy, unchanged. Bose told Proactive that Chevron will retain operatorship of PEL 82 with a 55% participating interest, while QatarEnergy will hold 25%. Custos Energy retains its 10% interest in the licence, and Sintana maintains a 49% indirect interest in Custos. As a result, Sintana's indirect exposure to PEL 82 remains unchanged following the transaction. Through Custos, Sintana continues to participate in the exploration potential of the licence alongside its joint venture partners. The company said it looks forward to further evaluating and demonstrating the potential of PEL 82 as exploration activities progress. PEL 82 is located offshore Namibia in the Walvis Basin and covers Blocks 2112B and 2212A. The licence spans approximately 11,450 square kilometres, with water depths ranging from 350 to 2,300 metres. Existing seismic data covers approximately 70% of the licence area, providing a substantial technical dataset for exploration planning. Previous drilling on the licence includes the Wingat-1 and Murombe-1 wells. Chariot Ltd (AIM:CHAR, OTC:OIGLF) CEO Adonis Pouroulis spoke with Proactive's Stephen Gunnion about the company's second Angolan transaction and its strategy to build a cash-generative upstream business focused on oil production and revenue. Pouroulis said Chariot is increasing its exposure to oil production by supporting Etu Energias, which has signed an agreement to acquire interests in offshore Angola Blocks 14 and 14K from Chevron. Chariot has also signed a framework agreement with BW Energy and Etu Energias for technical and operational support, with Shell Western Supply and Trading providing acquisition debt funding. The deal follows February's transaction involving Etu Energias and Azule Energy interests in the same blocks, which gave Chariot an economic interest equivalent to circa 4,000 barrels of oil per day. The latest deal is expected to add another 4,000 bpd, taking total exposure to circa 8,000 bpd. Pouroulis highlighted the established production profile of Blocks 14 and 14K - currently around 40,000 bpd - the licence extension to 2038, and upside from recent discoveries and existing infrastructure. "This isn't an exploration risk. This is revenue now," he said, pointing to "considerable running room and upside" in the licence. He also discussed Chariot's wider shift towards producing assets, summed up as "more barrels, more revenues." The first Angola deal is expected to close in H2 2026, with the latest closing in Q1 2027, subject to regulatory approvals. Pouroulis also reiterated the importance of the Anchois gas discovery in Chariot's Lixus concession offshore Morocco, saying the company continues to examine development opportunities. headline: Sintana Energy agrees PEL 90 interest transfer to chevron affiliate for $11M upfront
<<<SUMMARY>>>
Sintana Energy CEO Robert Bose joined Steve Darling from Proactive to discuss a new agreement involving Petroleum Exploration Licence 90 (PEL 90) in Namibia, following an announcement by Trago Energy regarding an agreement with Harmattan Energy Limited, an affiliate of Chevron. Under the agreement, Trago Energy will transfer its entire 10% participating interest in PEL 90 to Harmattan Energy. Sintana Energy maintains an indirect 49% interest in Trago, providing Sintana with continued exposure to the licence and its future exploration and development potential. As part of the transaction, Trago will receive US$11 million in cash upon completion. The agreement also provides for additional contingent consideration tied to the achievement of certain appraisal and production milestones. Importantly, the contingent consideration includes revenues associated with potential commercial production, which is currently estimated to involve between 1.5 million and 2.5 million barrels of oil. Bose said the transaction demonstrates Sintana’s strategy of reducing the capital requirements and downside exposure associated with its exploration portfolio while retaining exposure to potential upside if high-impact exploration projects progress successfully through appraisal and into production. By transferring the participating interest to a major industry participant while securing upfront cash and potential future milestone payments, Sintana believes the arrangement can provide value from PEL 90 without requiring the company to carry the same level of capital commitments associated with maintaining a direct participating interest. Attention now turns to the highly anticipated Nabba 1-X exploration well on PEL 90. The well represents another opportunity to test the prospectivity of the Orange Basin, one of the most closely watched exploration regions along the Atlantic margin. Bose highlighted the significance of maintaining capital-free exposure to PEL 90 and its exploration potential, particularly given the licence’s location within the broader Orange Basin and its proximity to major discoveries including Mopane and Venus. The transaction adds another element to Sintana’s strategy of maintaining exposure to high-impact exploration while seeking to manage capital requirements across its portfolio. The company continues to hold interests across its Atlantic margin assets, with PEL 90 providing exposure to a region that has attracted significant industry attention following major exploration successes. #proactiveinvestors #sintanaenergyinc #tsxv #sei #otcqb #seusf #Namibia #PEL90 #Chevron #OrangeBasin #Nabba #OilExploration #OilAndGas #Energy #Petroleum #Exploration #OffshoreEnergy #OilDiscovery #EnergyInvesting #NaturalResources #AtlanticMargin #OilStocks #ResourceStocks

headline: What High Diesel Prices Mean for These 5 Energy Stocks
<<<SUMMARY>>>
High diesel prices driven by a Strait of Hormuz supply disruption are benefiting energy companies differently. Marathon Petroleum, a pure-play refiner, is the biggest winner as it directly profits from the crack spread between crude costs and refined fuel prices. Integrated majors Chevron and ExxonMobil see meaningful but smaller gains across their larger businesses. Pipeline operators Energy Transfer and Enterprise Products Partners benefit modestly through increased volume fees, with their appeal primarily tied to steady dividend yields rather than diesel price exposure.
<<<INSIGHTS>>>
MPC | positive | Most direct beneficiary of high diesel prices as a pure refiner. Refining margins doubled to $36.33/barrel in Q2 2026, and refining segment EBITDA jumped to $6.7B from $1.9B year-over-year. However, sentiment is tempered by the caveat that margins are cyclical and will eventually normalize.
CVX | positive | Integrated major with significant downstream earnings boost. Q2 2026 downstream earnings jumped to $4.9B from $737M year-over-year due to stronger diesel and gasoline margins. Benefits from crack spread but with cushioning from other business segments.
ET | neutral | Fee-based pipeline operator with ~90% of business from take-or-pay contracts. Benefits minimally from diesel price spikes since it collects tolls regardless of commodity prices. Primary investment appeal is steady dividend yield (6.57%), not diesel exposure.
EPD | neutral | Similar to Energy Transfer, a fee-based infrastructure operator with similar profit structure from long-term contracts. No direct lift from diesel crack spreads. Value proposition centers on steady toll income and high distribution yields rather than commodity price movements.

headline: Oil Price is Still High: Boon for Chord Energy's Upstream Business?
<<<SUMMARY>>>
Chord Energy (CHRD) raised its 2026 oil production guidance twice to 162,500 barrels per day, driven by improved well performance and drilling efficiency in the Bakken region. With WTI crude trading above $80 per barrel, CHRD and other major oil producers like Chevron and ConocoPhillips are well-positioned to benefit from elevated commodity prices. CHRD trades at a significant valuation discount (2.48X EV/EBITDA vs. industry average of 9.88X) and has gained 50.4% over the past year.
<<<INSIGHTS>>>
CHRD | positive | Company raised production guidance twice, demonstrating operational improvements and confidence in future output. Trading at significant valuation discount relative to industry peers, with strong year-over-year stock performance and Zacks Rank #1 rating.
CVX | positive | Benefits from high oil prices with growing production volumes from Permian operations, positioning the company well to capitalize on elevated crude prices.
COP | positive | Generates significant revenues from crude oil and has low-cost drilling opportunities across Permian, Eagle Ford, and Bakken regions with bright long-term outlook for upstream operations.
<<<END>>>
